title: Multi-stage Rocket Simulations
description: At Rocket Propulsion Laboratory at UC San Diego, I helped create and build a CAD file using OpenRocket for the Osiris rocket team and our summer two-stage proof-of-design project. I did this in collaboration with both of our hardware avionics and staging teams. Using this CAD file, I ran simulations to help our staging team make important design decisions.

title: Blueraven Avionics
description: For the SET rocket launch with Rocket Propulsion Laboratory, I was the responsible engineer for the fail-safe avionics kit. In the case that something went wrong during launch, we used a Blueraven Altimeter kit to ensure that staging and recovery actuates regardless of the state of our custom in-house avionics kit was functioning.

title: Telemetry and Staging Avionics Kit Schematics
description: At Rocket Propulsion Laboratory at UC San Diego, created a KiCAD file to help design and export a schematic for our avionics kit which would handle capturing telemetry data as well as firing our staging mechanism through e-matches in a previous iteration of our rocket's design.

title: Speaker
description: In an electrical engineering class at UC San Diego, I worked with another student to build a functional phone speaker on a breadboard. We soldered a switch and a speaker to stripped wires that could be then plugged into our circuit breadboard and receive signal input from our phones through a stripped male headphone jack that could also plug into our breadboard. It was battery powered using a 9V battery block.

title: L1-sized Avionics Kit (2025-26)
description: Joining the Daedalus program at UC San Diego was my first experience as an engineer. During my time in Daedalus with Rocket Propulsion Laboratory at UC San Diego, I built an original avionics kit designed to withstand flight, record apogee, and return valuable telemetry.

title: Line-Following Robot (2026)
description: For an electrical engineering class at UC San Diego, I worked in a team of four to build a self-driving robot that would follow highlighted lines using PID design and photoresistors.
